subject: Copywriting
title: SEO: Writing for Algorithms
description: A micro-lesson that makes SEO: Writing for Algorithms usable.

hook.text: In the early 2000s, copywriters discovered that Google ranked pages by keywords. Writing for robots began.

buildup.text: Early SEO was keyword stuffing. Pages repeated 'cheap flights' 50 times. It was unreadable but it ranked.

discovery.text: Google's algorithm evolved. Now it rewards clear, helpful writing. Good copy and good SEO finally aligned.

twist.text: AI-generated SEO content flooded the web. Google responded by ranking human expertise higher.

climax.text: The best SEO copy sounds like a smart human talking. The algorithm learned to prefer what readers prefer.

punchline.text: Write for humans. The algorithm will follow.

quiz.question: What was early SEO copywriting focused on?

details.summary: Search Engine Optimization birthed a new copywriting discipline: writing for algorithms and humans simultaneously. SEO copy must include target keywords naturally while remaining engaging and useful. The tension between algorithmic requirements and human readability defined a new era of...
details.whyItMatters: SEO copywriting is the most widely practiced form of commercial writing today. Every website, blog, and product page must satisfy both search algorithms and human readers.
takeaways: SEO copy must serve two audiences: search algorithms and human readers
Keyword stuffing gave way to natural, user-focused content
Google's algorithm updates increasingly reward genuine quality over tricks

faq.question: How has SEO copywriting evolved?
faq.answer: Early SEO rewarded keyword stuffing — cramming target phrases into text regardless of readability. Google's algorithm updates (Panda, Penguin, and later AI-driven systems) increasingly penalize thin content and reward genuinely useful, well-written copy. Good writing and good SEO converged.

faq.question: Is SEO copywriting dying?
faq.answer: It's evolving, not dying. As AI search summaries and featured snippets change how people find information, SEO copy must adapt. But the fundamental skill — writing content that answers searcher intent while being technically discoverable — remains essential.
